hero.title: Crankshaft Failure UK Repair Cost, Engine Knock & Replacement
hero.description: Crankshaft failure is one of the most serious engine failures. A deep knocking noise isn't a minor issue — it's the sound of your engine destroying itself from the inside. If caught early (bearing wear only), you might get away with £800–£1,500 . If the crank journal is damaged or the crank snaps, engine replacement is almost always the only viable option.

cards.title: How Fast Can Damage Escalate?
cards.text: What starts as a slight knock can quickly lead to catastrophic engine failure. Catching the failure early is critical.
cards.fullText: Symptom to cost escalation How Fast Can Damage Escalate? What starts as a slight knock can quickly lead to catastrophic engine failure. Catching the failure early is critical. 01 Early Symptoms Knocking, low oil pressure, unusual noises. Worn main or rod bearings. £800+ 02 Continued Driving Increased wear and internal damage to bearings. Crank surface scored. £1,200+ 03 Severe Damage Crankshaft wear, metal debris, loss of performance. Rebuild required. £3,000+ 04 Engine Failure Crankshaft snapped or block damage (connecting rod exited block). £5,500+

cards.title: What Should You Do After a Crankshaft Failure?
cards.text: A step-by-step guide to making the right decision based on specialist consensus.
cards.fullText: Action Protocol What Should You Do After a Crankshaft Failure? A step-by-step guide to making the right decision based on specialist consensus. 01 Stop & Diagnose If you notice knocking or low oil pressure, stop driving and get a professional diagnosis. Deep knock isn't minor. 02 Assess the Damage A specialist will inspect the engine to determine the extent of crankshaft and bearing wear (sump off inspection). 03 Compare Options Review repair, rebuild or replacement costs and get quotes from trusted specialists across our network. 💡 The sooner you act, the lower the potential cost. Continuing to drive a damaged engine can lead to complete failure and a far more expensive repair.

items.title: How Bad Can It Get?
items.description: From early wear to complete engine failure — here's how the costs escalate exponentially.

blocks.text: Bearing wear - soft bearing material worn, oil starvation begins
Journal damage - crank surface scored, oversized bearings required
Crank crack - crankshaft cracked or snapped, engine cannot turn
Windowed block - connecting rod exits block, catastrophic loss

Real-world example from specialist forums (anonymised): 2014 Range Rover Sport SDV6, 92,000 miles. Owner ignored cold-start knock for 3 weeks. One morning, the engine made a loud bang and stopped. Connecting rod had exited the block. Total cost: £8,500 for a reconditioned engine fitted. The car was worth £14,000 - replacement was viable, but the owner regretted not investigating the knock earlier.

items.title: Avoiding Crankshaft Failure
items.description: Bearing failure is almost always caused by oil starvation or oil degradation. Follow these specialist recommendations.

cards.title: Regular Oil Changes
cards.text: Use manufacturer-spec oil (Land Rover: 5W30 C1/C2, BMW: LL04, Ford: WSS-M2C913-D).
cards.fullText: 01 Regular Oil Changes Use manufacturer-spec oil (Land Rover: 5W30 C1/C2, BMW: LL04, Ford: WSS-M2C913-D).

cards.title: Never Ignore Low Pressure
cards.text: Even a momentary flicker is a red flag — stop driving and investigate immediately.
cards.fullText: 02 Never Ignore Low Pressure Even a momentary flicker is a red flag — stop driving and investigate immediately.

cards.title: Listen for Cold-Start Knocks
cards.text: A deep knock that disappears after 1-2 seconds is still an indicator of bearing wear.

items.title: Frequently Asked Questions
items.description: Common questions answered regarding crankshaft failures, repairs, and replacement costs.

blocks.question: How much does crankshaft repair cost in the UK? +
blocks.answer: Bearing replacement (caught early): £800-£1,500. Crankshaft regrind / machining: £1,200-£2,000. Engine replacement (catastrophic failure): £2,700-£10,000+ depending on engine and condition. Labour: 15-25+ hours at £65-£95/hr (independent). Engine replacement cost guide

blocks.question: Can a snapped crankshaft be repaired? +
blocks.answer: No. A snapped or cracked crankshaft cannot be repaired. The only solution is a replacement engine (reconditioned, used, or rebuilt). On lower-value vehicles, this often means scrapping the car.

blocks.question: What causes crankshaft failure? +
blocks.answer: Most common causes: oil starvation (low oil level, oil pump failure), oil degradation (missed service intervals), bearing material fatigue (common on Land Rover TDV6/SDV6 from 80k-140k miles), or manufacturing defect (rare).

blocks.question: Which engines have the most crankshaft problems? +
blocks.answer: Based on 2025 quote data and KNOWN FAILURE PATTERNS: Land Rover 306DT SDV6/TDV6 (980 requests), Land Rover 276DT (700 requests), BMW N57D30 (830 requests). [EM-VERIFIED]

blocks.question: Is crankshaft failure covered under warranty? +
blocks.answer: On reconditioned engines, warranty typically covers internal component failure including crankshaft and bearings (12-24 months). Pre-existing damage or failure caused by oil starvation/oil neglect is not covered. Engines Market does not provide warranties - we are a comparison platform. Engine warranty guide

blocks.question: My car is worth £4,000 and has a crankshaft knock - what should I do? +
blocks.answer: If repair cost exceeds £2,500-£3,000, evaluate scrap value first. A reconditioned engine may cost £3,000-£5,000 fitted - often more than the car's value. Consider a used engine (£1,500-£2,500 fitted) if the car is otherwise sound, or scrap the vehicle and replace it.
